quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Every time you change lanes.
Only at night.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Do this even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you ride?

options.text: Anywhere in the lane.
Near the shoulder.
Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is usually the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so they are more likely to see you there.

questions.question: What makes a helmet provide the best protection?

options.text: It meets Department of Transportation standards.
It looks strong.
It is cheap.
It is your favorite color.

questions.correctAnswerText: It meets Department of Transportation standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no visible damage.

questions.question: Can a car and motorcycle share a lane?

options.text: Yes, they may share a lane.
Yes, but only in heavy traffic.
Yes, but only on weekends.
No, they should not share a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they should not share a lane.
questions.explanation: Both cars and motorcycles need a full lane width to operate safely. Lane sharing is not allowed.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride directly beside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting.
Other drivers may need that lane.
It is hard to see behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver will not see you. Also, the vehicle could block your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing gloves?

options.text: They make control easier.
They help other drivers see you.
They improve your grip on the handlebars.
They offer no protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: They improve your grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Even though a motorcycle is narrow, what does it still need?

options.text: A full lane width to operate safely.
Permission to share a lane with a car for short distances.
To share a lane with a car in heavy traffic.
The right to ride on the shoulder when traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: A full lane width to operate safely.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane width to operate safely, even though they are small. Lane sharing is not allowed.

questions.question: How does a passenger affect motorcycle handling?

options.text: A passenger makes no difference.
It is usually safe for new riders.
A passenger changes how the motorcycle handles.
Passengers help riders learn different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: A passenger changes how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: What is often in the center of the lane?

options.text: A landing strip.
An oily or greasy strip.
Lane markings.
Ice.

questions.explanation: Oil and grease from cars form a strip in the center of each lane. It is usually still safe for motorcycles unless the road is wet.

questions.question: What kind of pants protect a motorcycle rider best?

options.text: Soft pants.
Pants made of heavy material.
Loose pants that flap in the wind.
Short pants that expose legs.

questions.explanation: Wear pants that cover your entire legs and are made of leather or sturdy synthetic material. They should fit snugly without flapping, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is most likely a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white background and black letters show traffic rules like speed limits. Drivers must obey these regulatory signs.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they will distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers will see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. You need to know what is behind you at all times. Make mirror checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:

options.text: The owner's manual.
A general book about motorcycles.
Someone who has a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before riding it. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. The manual has information specific to your motorcycle.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller than most other vehicles.
Are very important to alert other motorists to a rider's intentions.
Should not be used if no vehicles are close to the motorcycle.
Are more complicated than those on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to alert other motorists to a rider's intentions.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signals every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is nearby. Signals are critical because motorcyclists are harder to see than other vehicles.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, motorcycle riders should watch out for:

options.text: Motorists looking for a place to park.
Cars leaving their parking spaces.
Oncoming traffic.
Noise.

questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked cars. A car may suddenly pull out into the road or leave its parking space.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ride faster to shake them.
Alert the local police.
Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Allow them to pass.

questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass. Change lanes safely to let them get ahead of you. Riding faster can make the situation more dangerous and does not solve the problem.
